findings.detail: `nextChoice` has exactly one production call site — CompositeTab.tsx:295 — and it passes `sourceChanged: false` literally. The `if (sourceChanged) return autoChoice(suggested)` branch (line 104) and the exported `manualChoice` helper are exercised only by tests/unit/compositeMapping.test.ts:115-116. Meanwhile the real "source changed" behaviour is reimplemented inline in the component: the `[fileData, compositeSheet]` effect does `setRetailPriceCol(suggest…)` + `setMappingSource(prev => ({...prev, retail: 'auto'}))`, and the `[fileData, rawSheet]` effect does the same for sku/cost/name. So the rule lives in two places, and the unit test asserting "another sheet or file: the new default replaces even a manual choice" is validating a code path the app never takes — if the component's inline version drifts, that test keeps passing. This is the code-smells handbook's dead-code entry (an exported path unreachable from production) plus a duplicated rule, not a user-visible bug.
findings.summary: nextChoice's `sourceChanged` branch and `manualChoice` are only reachable from tests

findings.detail: Observation, not a request. (1) A workbook with standard headers now arrives with Cost mapped, so `financialsEnabled` flips on and the export gains `Profit Analysis` + `Detailed BOM` sheets for users who previously got neither — and `Cost above Retail Price` becomes a validation error for them. (2) The Raw SKU dropdown no longer defaults to `Auto-Detect / All Columns`; once a column is auto-chosen, `SKU '…' missing` is checked against that column only, so a SKU that happens to appear in a Name cell now reports missing where it previously passed. Both are intentional, called out in docs/modules/MODULE_GUIDE.md under "Consequences, deliberate", and pinned by e2e cases (`the auto-chosen SKU column is what "SKU missing" checks`), and the existing hidden-content specs were correctly updated with `clearCost(page)` to preserve their old assertions. The reason this is worth a line: the escape hatch (clear Cost / re-select *Auto-Detect*) is discoverable only from the module guide, and the on-screen hint says "Columns marked Auto were chosen from the headers" without mentioning that this is what switched the extra sheets on. What would raise this above info is any user-facing surface that silently changes an exported artifact with no in-app explanation — adding half a sentence to the hint, or a line in the release notes, closes it.
findings.summary: Two deliberate behaviour changes for existing users; both documented, flagging for release notes
